sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cold-Chain Keg Wholesale and Export of Artisanal Hazy IPAs

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition with Anglo-American overlay in commercial, corporate, and foundation statutes)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 12 of 2017 (Articles 5-6 incorporation, Article 13 Resident Agent, Article 20 Protector, Article 32 liability); General Regulations of the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Private Interest Foundation Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado / Escritura Pública de Fundación)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 25 of 1995; the Foundation Charter must declare an initial patrimony (endowment), customarily USD 10,000 for banking credibility. No escrow or deposit receipt is required at incorporation; operational distribution capital must be evidenced in the foundation's own Panama bank account prior to licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Foundation Charter executed as Public Deed No. [•] of [date], inscribed under Entry No. [•] in the Private Interest Foundation Section of the Public Registry of Panama, is ratified as the Foundation's supreme instrument. RESOLVED, that the registered office at [address], Panama, and the Resident Agent, [law firm], are confirmed. RESOLVED, that [Name] is elected Foundation Council Chair and [Name] Secretary, authorized to open bank accounts, sign mandates, and procure commercial, sanitary, and environmental licenses for the craft-beer wholesale operations. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Protector with supervisory powers under Article 20 of Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED, that Council Members act jointly on distribution and licensing transactions, with Protector veto over the settlement of assets.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Registered Agent and Charter Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney or law firm acting as Resident Agent (required by Article 13 of Law 25 of 1995)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Resident Agent on the intended foundation name, registered office address, initial endowment, beneficiaries, Protector, and object (holding and operation of the craft-beer wholesale and microbrewery distribution vehicle). The Resident Agent drafts the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and verifies name availability at the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Bank reference letter issued within 3 months
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No registry filing occurs at this stage; if the Resident Agent queries the dossier, supply apostilled and certified English-to-Spanish translations or corrected corporate resolutions within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarized Execution of the Foundation Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the First Notarial Circuit of Panama (Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito, Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder or duly empowered attorney-in-fact appears before the notary together with the Resident Agent and executes the Foundation Charter as a public deed. The notary authenticates capacity and retains the original in the notarial protocol; two certified testimonios are issued for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Founder's passport and/or board resolutions of corporate founder
Notarized power of attorney (if signing by representative)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution due to defective clauses, amend the relevant charter articles through an addendum and reschedule execution; pre-inscription rejection carries no registry sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Private Interest Foundation Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File two certified testimonios of the public deed with the registry, accompanied by the Resident Agent's acceptance certificate and proof of payment of the registry tariff (approximately USD 150) at the Banco Nacional de Panamá. The registry examines name uniqueness, lawful object, declared endowment, and the appointment of the Council and Protector before granting entry.
required_dossiers: Testimonio No. 1 of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry queries (notas) are cured by filing a written correction request (subsanación) within 5 working days; if the query concerns deed content, execute an amending public deed and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Certificate and Certified Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Certification Directorate (Dirección de Certificaciones)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the entry of inscription, request the Certificado de Fundación (Foundation Certificate) and a certified copy of the registered deed. These instruments evidence legal personality and are prerequisites for RUC application, bank account opening, and licensing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, escalate through the Registro Público user attention window and confirm payment of all tariffs; obtain an interim good-standing letter from the registry.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online portal: 'Sede Electrónica de la DGI' (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa) and the 'Tramita Panamá' interoperable e-government platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned private interest foundation (PIF) not engaged in local business must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from the DGI prior to invoicing any Panamanian-source activity. The procedure is: (i) register the foundation with the Mercantile Registry; (ii) appoint a resident legal representative (agente residente); (iii) present the public deed and clean certificate (personería jurídica), apostilled or notarized in country of origin; (iv) file the DGI registration form (Formulario 11 / Digital Registration) with proof of address and representative's ID; (v) receive the RUC. For export-only activities, the RUC must be activated for ITBMS and export clearance; alternatively, an SEC license (Sociedad de Comercio Exterior) may be sought.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not offer a U.S.-style check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch election. The applicable elections are: (i) the Small Taxpayer Regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) for gross income ≤B/.11,000 (or ≤B/.35,000 as updated) allowing simplified filing; (ii) the Empresa de Comercio Exterior (SEC) regime under Law 28 of 1995 granting a 100% ITBMS exemption on export activity and reduced final income tax on export income; (iii) the Optional Advance Pricing Agreement / tax certainty regime; (iv) election to be treated as a foreign sales or logistics entity under the Zona Libre de Colón legal framework. A PIF may elect on the DGI registration form whether it will be subject to the '$300 annual franchise tax' (Impuesto Anual de Fundación) and remain passive versus be registered as an active export trader.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's VAT/GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for general ITBMS registration; any person habitually engaging in commercial, industrial, agricultural or service activities must register. A simplified small-taxpayer threshold of B/.11,000 (Panamanian Balboas, pegged 1:1 to USD) annual gross receipts determines simplified invoicing and quarterly payment, rather than exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates digital invoicing for all RUC holders. Since 2022, the DGI's 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá' requires electronic invoices (facturas electrónicas) to be transmitted in XML/JSON format via the SFE portal or accredited API; each invoice receives a unique 3D barcode (código de seguridad) only after real-time DGI validation. In addition, the 'Facturación Gratuita' web tool is available for small taxpayers. Retail and distribution invoices must be cleared with 'Correlativo with Asignación de Folio' and export operations must use the ITBMS form 'Declaración de Exportador' with reference to the customs electronic exchange.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating applies to (i) actual exportation of movable goods leaving the national customs territory; (ii) services rendered to non-residents that are physically performed outside Panama or used wholly abroad, including international transport; and (iii) goods sold to states, diplomatic missions and certain bonded export processing zones. The exporter must be registered as an exporter in the DGI and have filed a customs export declaration; the billing must show 0% ITBMS and the 'export' wording.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Mercancías) sealed by the National Customs Authority
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical exit of the craft beer consignment
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa al Exterior) from a Panamanian bank evidencing FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and National Customs Authority conduct ex-post review of zero-rated export declarations, cross-matching the digital invoice, customs manifest, and banking remittance certificate. Failure to substantiate physical export or FX repatriation within 180 days results in retroactive liquidation of ITBMS at 7%, plus late interest (1.25% per month) and increasing surcharges (10%-150% depending on good faith); deliberate fabrication of export evidence is tax fraud under Articles 968 and 969 of the Código Fiscal, punishable by imprisonment (1-5 years) and fines up to 3 times the evaded tax, plus cancellation of the exporter RUC and SEC privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama has no autonomous central bank. Monetary authority is distributed: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) supervises banks, fintechs and payment intermediaries; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent, clearing-house agent and operator of the national RTGS (ACH Panamá); the Panamanian Coin Commission (Comisión de Moneda) administers Balboa coin issue; and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) manages external financing. The U.S. dollar is the effective legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized territory: the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) circulates only as coins at a statutory 1:1 parity with the U.S. dollar; no paper PAB exists and exchange control legislation is absent. Both current account (trade payments, freight, insurance, royalties) and capital account (equity contributions, capital repatriation, dividend and profit remittance from a Private Interest Foundation) are fully convertible with no prior central-bank authorization, no surrender of hard currency, and no profit-remittance permit. The only operative restrictions are SBP-regulated AML/KYC verification at the receiving bank, OFAC/UN sanctions screening, and compliance with Panama's territorial-source income tax and FATCA/CRS reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panamanian law imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to sell export receipts on a controlled market. Proceeds from craft beer exports (ISIC 4632) may be retained in USD or any convertible currency, whether in Panama or abroad. For tax and AML defense, the exporter must retain the DUA Siglo XXI customs declaration, commercial invoices, bills of lading, SWIFT credits and payment confirmations reflecting the receipt of funds within the accounting period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD current account with sub-ledgers for export collections and local distributor settlements)
Private-banking liquidity and wealth-linked PIF deposit account (USD)
Operational Account plus Trade Finance (Commercial LC issuance) and FX derivative capability

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC Credomatic (BAC International Bank, Inc., Panama Branch)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Recurring retail distribution settlement account and card-acceptance clearing for distributor network
Fiscal-agent clearing account; escrow-capable state-bank account for capital injections
Operational Account with robust correspondent banking access for SWIFT wires
Retail savings and escrow account; not suitable as PIF treasury concentration point

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW (auxiliary rail only). Legal constraints: under Panama's Financial Code and SBP rules implementing Law No. 23 of April 27, 2015 (AML/CFT) and Fintech Hub Law No. 25 of 2023, any electronic-money institution or cross-border digital wallet providing payment services to Panamanian residents or receiving settlement from Panamanian-domiciled entities must obtain SBP authorization or a fintech sandbox license. Offshore EMIs (e.g., UK EMD agents, European EMI licenses) cannot act as the principal treasury or concentration account for the PA_PIF structure without violating placement rules and creating de-risking exposure. Use an offshore EMI only as a low-balance, sweeper-connected collection point for retail e-commerce beer sales, with mandatory daily sweeps to an SBP-licensed commercial bank and full reconciliation of merchant-of-record documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De jure SBP Customer Due Diligence rules require identification of the founder, all council members (Consejo de la Fundación), the Protector, the Resident Agent and the ultimate beneficial owners. De facto, tier-1 commercial banks require at least one in-person appearance in Panama by a designated signatory council member for final account activation; remote opening is possible only under private-bank programs (e.g., Towerbank, BAC) using notarized and apostilled board resolutions, video-interview affirmation, and pre-funded source-of-wealth reports. Banco Nacional de Panamá and Caja de Ahorros unconditionally mandate physical attendance of a council member and the Resident Agent at the onboarding interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation lacking demonstrable economic substance in Panama (no physical office, no management meetings held in-country, no payroll).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Resident-agent service agreement; notarized office lease in Panama City; employment contracts and payroll records for local management; minutes of foundation council meetings held in Panama; warehouse or cold-chain storage lease proving craft-beer distribution operations; annual substance filing and sworn financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure—PIF by law may leave beneficiaries unnamed and banks reject blind structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn private instrument listing beneficiaries and protectors; consolidated organizational chart of the brewery group; passport copies of all natural-person beneficiaries; audited financial statements of the ultimate brewery parent; documentation of the founder's original wealth; proof of the initial endowment chain (bank statements and transfer confirmations).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP/geographic exposure—trade flows via high-risk jurisdictions or settlement attempted in cryptocurrency or cash.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Closed-loop documentary trade package (commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, full-set bills of lading, DUA Siglo XXI export declaration); positive OFAC/UN/EU/UK sanctions screening reports; a written treasury policy prohibiting cash and crypto payments; the PIF's approved SBP-compliant AML/CFT manual and designated compliance officer certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF as a layer for IP/royalty sheltering or tax evasion—banks flag a foundation receiving brewing-related royalties without operational activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation deed and bylaws evidencing legitimate proprietary and commercial purposes; executed trademark/brewery license agreements with arm's-length royalty rates; territorial-source tax opinion from Panamanian counsel; tax-residency certificates of beneficiaries; CRS/FATCA registration confirmations; bank-confirmed records that distribution and cold-chain logistics revenues, not passive royalties, drive the account flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) The foundation council passes a formal board resolution authorizing the capital contribution (Aporte Patrimonial) to the PIF's designated USD operating account; (2) the remitter executes a SWIFT MT103 from its home-country bank with a valid SWIFT Category Purpose Code (e.g., GCPC for general cross-border payment) and the beneficiary field matching exactly the PIF name and bank profile as held on file; Panama does not use IBAN, so the beneficiary account must cite the bank's SWIFT BIC plus the local account number and bank branch; (3) no central-bank approval or exchange-control permit is required—the receiving SBP-licensed bank verifies the KYC file and credits the proceeds immediately; (4) the recipient bank records the wire as 'founder contribution' for FATCA/CRS classification, and the PIF issues a Carta de Aporte with substantiating board minutes for the audit trail; (5) retain for defense: signed contribution resolution, founder's remitting account statements, apostilled foundation charter, passport copies of all council members and beneficiaries, and the founder's source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are segmented by purpose: (a) international supplier payments for malt, hops, kegs and cold-chain equipment—SWIFT MT103 with full remitter and beneficiary details, or a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) issued by Banistmo or BAC Credomatic against presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, transport document and MINSA sanitary certificate; (b) regional export collections from Colombian and Central American craft-beer distributors—documentary collections (CAD) and confirmed LCs in USD to eliminate currency conversion; (c) domestic micro-distributor settlements—ACH Panamá local clearing and Real-Time Electronic Transfer (TEF) rails for same-day cold-chain payment execution; (d) intra-group remittances to the brewery parent—clean SWIFT MT103 supported by an intercompany services agreement and transfer-pricing documentation showing the foundation's profit margin as a distribution intermediary. Export proceeds may remain offshore; however, all outbound disbursements must retain the underlying customs and logistics documents to support Panama's territorial-source tax position and to avoid artificial base-erosion adjustments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) with SBP-licensed commercial banks to hedge European malt and equipment purchase payables.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) to hedge regional distribution receivables without requiring physical hard-currency conversion.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR, USD/COP) for large capital expenditures such as EU-sourced brewery production equipment or acquisition of cold-chain assets.

Plain-vanilla currency options (puts/calls) on EUR/USD and GBP/USD, permitted only where the PIF's treasury committee has adopted a written derivatives-use policy and the counterparty bank is authorized by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Fee (Annual Franchise Tax / Anualidad de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before 31 December of each calendar year; no extension is available. Fee tier is assessed on the foundation's net asset value as recorded in the foundation instrument and accounting ledger: assets up to US$10,000 = US$350; assets between US$10,001 and US$1,000,000 = US$600; assets exceeding US$1,000,000 = US$2,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers the statutory Registry surcharge on the unpaid fee and an administrative fine of up to US$300; sustained non-payment for two consecutive calendar years may lead to administrative strike-off, loss of good-standing certification, cancellation of the foundation registration, and resignation of the registered agent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Formulario DGI 210) – full return for Panama-source commercial distribution income, or nil/informative return where all income is sourced outside Panama under the territorial tax regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually within the DGI-scheduled calendar window for the corresponding tax year, generally 1 January through 31 March of the succeeding year; large taxpayers may be extended to 30 April. Quarterly advance payments follow Form 310 due-date rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing triggers a statutory surcharge of up to 20% of the tax due, monthly interest of 1.5% under the Tax Code, administrative fines of up to US$5,000, denial of the Certificado de Cumplimiento (tax compliance certificate), and potential criminal tax liability for fraudulent statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CRS / FATCA Annual Reporting Return (nil or substantive automatic-exchange filing under OECD Common Reporting Standard and US FATCA intergovernmental framework)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – International Tax Affairs and Automatic Exchange of Information Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 April immediately following the reporting calendar year; CRS classification and registration changes must be updated within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a nil or substantive CRS/FATCA return carries administrative penalties of up to US$1,000 per year, suspension of the foundation's tax compliance certificate, and AML-type sanctions under Law 23 of 2015 in cases of willful omission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No audit is compulsory for a Private Interest Foundation solely because of its legal form. A certified independent audit by a Panamanian Contador Público Autorizado becomes mandatory when (i) the foundation derives Panama-source gross commercial revenue from the craft-beer distribution business at or above the DGI audited-statement threshold (approximately US$3,000,000 of annual gross sales or US$2,000,000 of total assets, per DGI Form 210 filing instructions), (ii) the Foundation Charter, Regulations, or a resolution of the Foundation Council imposes an audit obligation, or (iii) the registered agent's AML compliance program or a commercial lender requires audited accounts for enhanced due diligence. Otherwise, unaudited accounting records are sufficient for the annual Registry fee and territorial income-tax filings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Panama governs any audited or tax-basis financial statements; a simplified cash-basis record system is permitted for a foundation without Panama-source commercial activity. The foundation must at all times maintain records sufficient to identify the assets, liabilities, income, and expenditure of the patrimonial estate under Law 25 of 1995.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT) as applied to obliged non-financial subjects, the registered agent must identify, verify, and retain current beneficial-ownership information for the foundation and re-confirm such information on a 12-month cycle measured from client on-boarding. Any transfer of foundation interest certificates, change of beneficiaries, amendment of the Foundation Council, or modification of the foundation regulations must be evidenced by notarized written instruments, reflected in the Council resolutions and the internal UBO ledger, and reported to the registered agent within 30 days. Panama does not operate a public UBO registry; the private UBO ledger held by the registered agent is the authoritative record and must be produced to the Public Registry or the Financial Analysis Unit upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members and Officers
Register of Foundation Interests, Beneficiaries, and Transfer Ledger
Minutes Book of the Foundation Council and Guardian (Protector), if appointed

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800–US$2,500 per annum for a Panama registered agent and registered office, including compliance, UBO ledger maintenance, and bank-signature support; notarial compilation and translation fees are billed separately.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 where no audit is required; US$5,000–US$15,000 for a certified Panamanian CPA audit of a commercially active craft-beer distribution foundation with inventory, receivables, and cross-border sales.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory ISR rate of 25% on Panamanian-source net income under Article 699 of the Fiscal Code. The territorial system excludes foreign-source income derived from commercial activity performed and perfected abroad; export sales (FOB/DAP/CFR) of craft beer to non-resident buyers where negotiation, title passage and delivery occur outside Panama may fall outside the ISR base, whereas domestic wholesale distribution to Panamanian importers, bars, restaurants and supermarkets remains taxable. No statutory tax holiday applies to standard distribution activity; SEM (Multinational Headquarters) and Free Zone regimes are unavailable to a non-qualifying PIF. A purely asset-holding foundation pays only the fixed annual PAB 300 foundation tax under Law 25 of 1995, but a PIF conducting Panamanian-source distribution is fully subject to the 25% ISR.
